english.title: Communicate information regarding noxious substance - hoax - terrorism
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) communicated information, namely **(..SPECIFY..), which you knew or believed to be false, intending to induce in a person anywhere in the world a belief that a noxious substance or other noxious thing was likely to be present in any place and thereby endanger human life or create a serious risk to human health
english.legislation: Contrary to section 114(2) and (3) of the Anti-Terrorism, Crime and Security Act 2001.

english.notes: Terrorist connection - this offence is listed in Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 2020. Where the court has determined that there is a terrorist connection, the court has to treat this as an aggravating factor in sentencing (section 69 of that Act) and the notification requirements under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 apply (section 42 of that Act). In addition, section 23A of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides for forfeiture of money or other property.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
